proof_summary: The numerator valuation is \(\sum_{i\ge1}\lfloor m/p^i\rfloor^2\), obtained by counting ordered pairs whose gcd is divisible by each \(p^i\); Legendre’s formula similarly expands the denominator valuation, and the bound \(\sum_j j\lfloor M/j\rfloor\le M^2\) proves exact divisibility so the quotient valuation is their difference. When \(m=np+k\) with \(k<p\), every \(\lfloor m/p^i\rfloor\) agrees with its value at \(np\); this preserves all old denominator terms, while each newly added index gives factorial argument \(1\) and hence zero valuation, so both valuations are separately constant.
